title: Is AI on your power bill?
summary: AI data centers need huge amounts of electricity. A Senate report, a bipartisan bill and the companies disagree about who pays for the grid upgrades.

say: Your electricity bill might be helping pay for AI.
One 100-megawatt data center can use as much power as about 100,000 homes.
Permanent jobs? About 100, says a report from Senate Democrats.
scenes.label: One 100 MW data center

say: Grid upgrades are often split among everyone with a meter.
A Harvard expert told NPR: everyone pays.
scenes.credit: Ari Peskoe, Harvard Electricity Law Initiative, to NPR

say: In Louisiana, estimates say one Meta project could add 8 to 13 dollars a month to the average Entergy bill.
scenes.title: ELECTRIC BILL

say: The report says none of seven big companies agreed to pay for upgrades built only for them.
The companies say they pay their direct costs.

left.says: None of 7 companies agreed to pay for upgrades built only for them

right.says: They pay their direct costs. Bigger upgrades help everyone.

say: Now a bipartisan Senate bill would make new data centers pay the extra grid costs they add.
scenes.head: U.S. SENATE · BILL
scenes.title: Data centers pay their own way
lines: New data centers of 20 MW or more
cover the extra grid costs they add

say: So, who should pay? Tell us below.
